text:
Olga: Heads-up, customer reported streaming chat in Safari (iOS 15 and macOS Safari 16) is starting then freezing after a few partial events. Chrome/FF work fine. No reconnects observed on the client, connection looks open but silent after ~10-20s.
Ella (Support): can you get the request headers and a short repro? Is there a CDN in front of them or only our api?
Olga: They said Cloudflare in front of their webapp, hosted api eu1. Client EventSource headers they sent:
  Accept: text/event-stream
  Cache-Control: no-cache
  Origin: https://app.customer.com
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
  withCredentials: true (using eventsource-polyfill)
Repro steps from customer: open page -> start stream -> see couple messages -> stream goes silent until refresh.
Sam (SRE): pull the server trace for that session id and look for flushes, idle timeouts, and any upstream closes. Also check edge headers and cf-cache-status.
Olga: server trace (sanitized):
  [stream] conn open id=abc123
  [stream] write chunk 180 bytes
  [stream] write chunk 432 bytes
  [stream] idle no-data for 14s
  [stream] upstream closed? code=0
We also got a cf-cache-status: HIT and later a 304 from Cloudflare on a reconnect attempt.
Tyler (Frontend): two common Safari pitfalls with SSE: cached responses or intermediate proxies returning 304s, and CORS misconfig when credentials are used. Safari sometimes keeps sockets half-open if a cache responds with 304 or strips chunked framing.
Ella (Support): what are the response headers we returned from our edge for the stream route?
Sam (SRE): current edge response headers:
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
  Transfer-Encoding: chunked
  Connection: keep-alive
  Cache-Control: max-age=0, must-revalidate, private
  Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
  Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
  Vary: Accept-Encoding
Note: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * + Allow-Credentials: true is invalid and will be ignored by browsers; Vary doesn't include Origin, and Cache-Control isn't explicitly no-store/no-cache for CDNs.
Olga: they are sending withCredentials so Access-Control should echo Origin, not "*".
Tyler (Frontend): also recommend Surrogate-Control: no-store to tell CDNs not to cache, and Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate plus Pragma: no-cache for older clients. Add Vary: Origin so caches key by origin. And send periodic keepalive comments (":keepalive\n\n") every ~3s to avoid proxy idle coalescing.
Sam (SRE): quick mitigation we can rollout on the edge: set headers for stream paths to:
  Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate
  Pragma: no-cache
  Surrogate-Control: no-store
  Vary: Origin, Accept-Encoding
  Access-Control-Allow-Origin: echo request Origin when credentials are present
  Cache-Control: no-transform
Also ensure the runtime flushes small chunks frequently and emits a newline-terminated comment every 3s.
Ella (Support): can we get the customer to run a minimal curl repro so we can see whether the edge emits continuous chunks and whether Cloudflare replies with 304?
Olga: sent them this curl:
  curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Origin: https://app.customer.com" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/stream"
Sam (SRE): i'll patch a staging canary with the header changes + keepalive and add a regression test that simulates a Cloudflare-like 304 on reconnect to ensure mobile Safari keeps receiving events.
deploy-bot: deploy staging stream-sse-headers-fix to eu1 scheduled at 2026-03-15T20:12:00Z
Olga: customer tried staging canary: desktop Safari fixed immediately; iOS Safari improved but still has intermittent stalls on older iOS builds. They attached a HAR: sequence shows initial 200 chunked, then CF returned HIT then a 304 on a small reconnect and browser idled the socket.
Tyler (Frontend): mobile safari TCP/TLS session reuse and aggressive optimization can exacerbate this. Extra guards: ensure no Content-Length is set, chunked transfer on, disable buffering on proxies (e.g., nginx: proxy_buffering off; add X-Accel-Buffering: no), and keep small chunk flushes (don't coalesce). Also include double newline after each event.
Ella (Support): immediate action list:
- Sam: push prod canary with Surrogate-Control/Cache-Control/Vary: Origin + keepalive flushes and add regression tests (ETA today EOD)
- Tyler: document SSE + Safari best practices and polyfill guidance for customers still on older iOS
- Ella: update KB and coordinate with customer to validate; supply signed canary endpoint if needed
Sam (SRE): pushed to prod canary. Monitor for cf-cache-status and cf-response codes. If Cloudflare still returns 304 we may need an edge rule to bypass cache by adding Cache-Control or query param to force pass-through.
Olga: customer confirmed prod canary eliminated desktop stalls and reduced iOS failures to <1% across their fleet; a few legacy iOS devices still need polyfill fallback. Closing after QA. Thanks all :tada:
